title: Terrace configuration contract, envelope version 1
description: The document an image publishes saying what configuration it takes. Normative prose is in FORMAT.md; this file is what a producer is checked against and what a consumer may validate before reading. Objects here are deliberately open — the format evolves by addition, and a consumer that ignores what it does not recognise stays correct. Producer typos are caught by the conformance corpus, not by this file.

terrace_contract.description: The version of this envelope's shape. A consumer refuses a version it was not written against rather than reading it optimistically.

producer.title: Which implementation wrote this document
producer.description: Not a fact about the configuration. `loader` is what makes every `text_constraint` in the document safe to apply: those patterns were measured against a named library's environment reads, and another library has different answers. A consumer that does not recognise the loader must not apply the reads in FORMAT.md.

name.description: The implementation, e.g. `terrace-config`. A stable identifier, not a display name.

version.description: The implementation's own version. Not `app.version`, which versions the service being described.

loader.description: The library whose environment reads the text constraints were measured against, e.g. `figment`. Named rather than restated: a vocabulary describing every way a binder might read a string is a language two implementations can disagree in.

app.title: Which build this contract describes
app.description: Every field moves independently of the configuration surface, which is why they are collected: a consumer diffing two contracts to see whether the configuration changed diffs everything except this.

revision.description: The commit the image was built from.

schema.title: Every key the loader can carry, in every spelling that can supply it
schema.description: Also the whole of what a producer's `json` rendering emits, so this subschema is addressable on its own as `contract.schema.json#schema`.

schema_version.description: The version of this half's shape, moving independently of `terrace_contract`. Version 2 added nesting inside `constraint`. A consumer gates on this before widening its keyword allowlist.

loader.description: The variables the loader reads to decide what the layers are, rather than to fill a key. Step 1 of the ordered read in FORMAT.md.

dialect.title: How a key path becomes a name in each layer

prefix.description: The environment namespace this contract governs, e.g. `PORTFOLIO_`. Never empty: a prefixless loader cannot tell its own namespace from the machine's, and every gate in FORMAT.md rests on that distinction.

nesting_separator.description: What separates path segments in an environment spelling, e.g. `__`.

indirection_suffix.description: What marks a variable as naming a file rather than holding a value, e.g. `_FILE`.

role.description: What the loader does with it. `other` is the degradation target for a role a reader does not know; a reader meeting it should say it skipped the variable rather than treat it as checked.

default.description: What the loader assumes when the variable is unset. Null when there is no default.

key.title: One configuration key, in every spelling that can supply it

path.description: The document path, e.g. `csp.cloudflare.turnstile`. Unique across `keys`.

env.description: The variable supplying it directly. Null means no variable names it, and `unreachable` says why.

env_file.description: The variable naming a file that holds it.

secrets_file.description: The file name inside the secrets directory that supplies it.

docs.description: Prose describing the key. Empty when there was none. Markdown; the first paragraph is the summary.

ty.description: The producer's own name for the field's type, with any optionality stripped — `required` already says whether the key may be left out. Token text in the producer's language, not a portable type name: read `constraint` to check a value, never this.

values.description: The fixed set of values the key accepts, spelled as the loader accepts them. Empty when the key is not a choice.

constraint.description: What the value must be once it is in the document, as JSON Schema keywords. Absent means no check is possible — a type the producer could not interpret — and a consumer must not invent one. Nests under `items` and `additionalProperties` from schema_version 2.

text_constraint.description: What the characters of an environment variable must be, before anything parses them. Complementary to `constraint`, never an alternative: a consumer checking a variable applies this to the raw text and `constraint` to whatever the parse produced. Measured against `producer.loader`.

aliases.description: Other document spellings of this key. A file using one loads, so a consumer must accept them.

env_aliases.description: The environment spellings of `aliases`, derived by the producer rather than left to a consumer — a derivation written as prose is one each consumer gets differently wrong.

default.description: The observed default, rendered for display. Null when the key has none. `<redacted>` for a secret.

default_value.description: The same default as a value rather than as text, for a consumer that wants to compare rather than print. Null when the key has none, which is indistinguishable from a default that is itself null — use `default` and `required` to tell those apart.

note.description: Prose qualifying the default, e.g. `permanent` for a zero that means no expiry.

required.description: Whether some layer must supply the key. Not JSON Schema's `required`, which asks whether one document carries it: a required secret is supplied by a mounted file and the rendered document does not carry it at all.

secret.description: Whether the value is a credential. A secret never carries a default, anywhere in the document.

reserved.description: Whether the loader reads it directly from the environment, before the layers exist. No file may supply it.

allOf.title: A key the environment cannot name says why
allOf.description: The two reasons differ in whether the environment can reach the key at all, and a consumer treating a bare null as `skip this key` is right for one and wrong for the other.

allOf.title: A secret carries no default
allOf.description: Refused at build time in either order the two were declared. This is the point the document crosses into a public registry.

text_form.description: How to read the characters a variable holds, before checking the result against `constraint`. Always present, so that a null `text_constraint` has one meaning: `text` says any text is fine, `unknown` says nothing could be determined. The read each form names belongs to `producer.loader`, not to this document.

unreachable.description: Why no environment variable is published for a key. `unnameable`: no variable names it, so the document is the only layer left. `indirection`: a name this schema gives another key also fills this one, which a producer refuses to publish.

json_schema.title: The same keys as a JSON Schema, for validating the document a chart renders
json_schema.description: The only half a stock validator acts on, and it carries no environment spellings at all. Draft-07 by default, because that is what Helm validates values.schema.json against.

external.title: The surface outside the loader's namespace
external.description: What else this image reads, and what it does not care about. A positive declaration rather than a suppression list: a declared variable is checked exactly like a configuration key, an ignored one may be misspelt freely.

ignore.description: Names nobody owns. Only a trailing `*` is a wildcard — every consumer implements this matching itself, and a pattern language is a place for two implementations to disagree about what is exempt from a check.

unknown.description: What to do with a variable no rule accounted for. Step 7 of the ordered read.

external_var.title: A variable this image reads that is nobody's configuration key

name.description: Never carries `dialect.prefix`: everything in that namespace is a configuration key, and declaring one external would leave it governed and exempt at once.

owner.description: What reads it — a toolchain, a base image, a library.
